free_tier.stated: 'Free accounts include 6 GB of storage, and Premium includes 10 TB.' Downstream is metered on every account: 'Free PikPak accounts have a daily Downstream limit of 20 GB, which resets at 0:00 Singapore Time. All Connected Apps together can use up to 25% of this daily limit, or 5 GB per day.'
free_tier.notes: Two counters, not one: 20 GB/day for the official apps and 5 GB/day for anything programmatic (WebDAV, CLI, MCP, personal access tokens). The 6 GB store is what the downloaded bytes must pass through, exactly as CloudPipe's 450 GB must pass through a 15 GB Google Drive.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated. No per-object number is published; the limits that bite on a free account are the 6 GB store and three Cloud Download tasks a day.
per_object_cap.notes: A 20 GiB object cannot be held in a 6 GB store at all, so the object cap is the store, not a published file limit.

retention.stated: files stay in the account until deleted, and the free account holds 6 GB, so retention is bounded by capacity rather than by a day count. Non-Premium accounts with no login for 12 consecutive months may be deleted.

egress.terms: Metered in three dimensions per calendar month: cloud download 40 TB, downstream 4 TB, upload 1 TB, then a separate free-account daily downstream cap of 20 GB. 'All Connected Apps together can use up to 25% of this daily limit, or 5 GB per day.' Over the limit 'Downstream traffic slows to about 100 KB/s' and 'New Cloud Download tasks are blocked'.
egress.free_allowance: 20 GB/day downstream in the official apps; 5 GB/day for Connected Apps

record.interface_detail: official apps plus WebDAV, an official CLI, an MCP server and personal access tokens, all grouped by the vendor as 'Connected Apps' and all subject to the 5 GB/day cap
record.tooling: rclone over WebDAV or the CLI; both land in the Connected Apps bucket and take the quarter allowance
record.chaining: Adds 150 GB a month to a no-card ladder for one email address, making it the largest per-signup free step that is not CloudPipe. Its counter resets daily, so it repeats in month two.

record.limits_note: The monthly 4 TB downstream quota is not the binding number for a free account; the daily cap is, by a factor of 120.
record.binding_note: At 5 GB/day a programmatic client gets 150 GB/month and at 20 GB/day an app-only client gets 600 GB/month. Both are below every other group-1 step except Bitport, and both require deleting through a 6 GB store.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is by email. No card and no phone is named on the help-centre pages read; the signup form itself was not opened, so this is the published gate rather than an observed one.

record.reliability_note: Over the daily cap downstream slows to about 100 KB/s and new cloud-download tasks are blocked while running ones continue; a free account with no login for 12 months may be deleted.
record.confidence_note: Both counters are vendor sentences read.

record.notes: The number that matters to the ladder is 150 GB/month programmatic, not 600: the service is driven with a script, and the vendor caps every programmatic path at 25% of the daily allowance.

card.summary: 6 GB free. Premium includes 10 TB base storage (expandable for purchase). No free route to >=500 GB: the free tier is 6 GB flat.

free_tier.stated: 6 GB free. Premium includes 10 TB base storage (expandable for purchase). No free route to >=500 GB: the free tier is 6 GB flat.

egress.terms: Metered twice over. Free accounts have a daily downstream quota; every account, free or paid, has a monthly Basic Transfer Quota, and 'Connected Apps share 25% of this daily allowance — up to 5 GB per day for all Connected Apps combined'. Downstream counts playback and previews, not just downloads.

record.tooling: Tier 1 rclone backend since v1.62, read-only for uploads? No. Backend supports read and write per rclone's table (ModTime R, hash md5). This is the crucial detail: rclone is classified as a 'Connected App', so it inherits the 5 GB/day cap.
record.chaining: Paid accounts offer up to 10 TB storage. Transfer limits restrict downloads to 5 GB per day via connected applications and 20 GB per day general downstream. Multiple accounts scale storage capacity while egress remains bound to individual daily quotas.

limits.value: reviews and online playback burn downstream quota, so scrape-style read patterns drain

record.limits_note: per-ip-shaping / pull-count hybrid: 20 GB/day downstream on free, 5 GB/day for all Connected Apps combined, monthly transfer quota on top. Free tier 6 GB storage. This provider is the cleanest illustration that quota and egress must be scored separately.
record.reliability_note: Transfer accounting is aggressive: previews and online playback burn downstream quota, so scrape-style read patterns drain it without any download. Price differs by region (US $4.99/mo Premium, Japan JPY 700, 'Global Premium' $9.99/mo).

egress.terms: HARD METERED, and worse for programmatic use. Verbatim from help centre: base quotas are 'Cloud Download: 40 TB per month. Downstream: 4 TB per month, including playback, previews, and downloads. Upload: 1 TB per month.' And 'Connected Apps share a combined transfer quota limit equal to 25% of your monthly Transfer Quota, across all three traffic dimensions.' So rclone/WebDAV/CLI. The only programmatic paths. Get 25% of 4 TB = 1 TB/month downstream.
